#!/bin/bash
ROOT=/bench/repo
mapfile -t ALL_GO < <(find "$ROOT" -name '*.go' -type f | sort)

declare -A CONTENTS
for f in "${ALL_GO[@]}"; do
  CONTENTS["$f"]=$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null)
done

# Extract internal symbols: path|pkg|kind|name|recv
SYMS=()
while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ "$file" == *_test.go ]] && continue
  content="${CONTENTS[$file]}"
  pkg=$(printf '%s' "$content" | awk '/^package /{print $2; exit}')
  [[ -z "$pkg" ]] && continue
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ -z "$line" ]] && continue
    SYMS+=("$line")
  done < <(printf '%s' "$content" | awk -v file="$file" -v pkg="$pkg" '
    /^func / {
      line=$0
      sub(/^func /,"",line)
      recv=""
      if (match(line,/^\([^)]*\)[[:space:]]+/)) {
        recv=substr(line,RSTART,RLENGTH)
        line=substr(line,RSTART+RLENGTH)
      }
      split(line,a,/[( ]/)
      name=a[1]
      if (name=="init") next
      if (name ~ /^(Test|Benchmark|Example|Fuzz)/) next
      kind="func"
      rtype=""
      if (recv!="") {
        kind="method"
        gsub(/^[[:space:]]*\(/,"",recv)
        gsub(/\)[[:space:]]*$/,"",recv)
        gsub(/^\*/,"",recv)
        split(recv,parts,/ /)
        rtype=parts[length(parts)]
      }
      print file"|"pkg"|"kind"|"name"|"rtype
    }')
done < <(find "$ROOT/internal" -name '*.go' -type f | sort)

count_pat() {
  local text="$1" pat="$2"
  printf '%s' "$text" | grep -oE "$pat" | wc -l
}

declare -A PKG_OF
for f in "${ALL_GO[@]}"; do
  PKG_OF["$f"]=$(printf '%s' "${CONTENTS[$f]}" | awk '/^package /{print $2; exit}')
done

results=()
for sym in "${SYMS[@]}"; do
  IFS='|' read -r file pkg kind name rtype <<< "$sym"
  fanin=0
  if [[ "$kind" == "func" ]]; then
    qpat="\\b${pkg}\\.${name}[[:space:]]*\\("
    upat="(^|[^[:alnum:]_\\.])${name}[[:space:]]*\\("
    for f in "${ALL_GO[@]}"; do
      text="${CONTENTS[$f]}"
      fpkg="${PKG_OF[$f]}"
      # qualified
      c=$(count_pat "$text" "$qpat")
      fanin=$((fanin + c))
      # unqualified same package
      if [[ "$fpkg" == "$pkg" ]]; then
        c=$(count_pat "$text" "$upat")
        fanin=$((fanin + c))
        if [[ "$f" == "$file" ]] && printf '%s' "$text" | grep -qE "^func ${name}[[:space:]]*\\("; then
          fanin=$((fanin - 1))
        fi
      fi
    done
  else
    mpat="\\.${name}[[:space:]]*\\("
    for f in "${ALL_GO[@]}"; do
      text="${CONTENTS[$f]}"
      c=$(count_pat "$text" "$mpat")
      fanin=$((fanin + c))
      if [[ "$f" == "$file" ]] && printf '%s' "$text" | grep -qE "^func \\([^)]*\\)[[:space:]]*${name}[[:space:]]*\\("; then
        fanin=$((fanin - 1))
      fi
    done
  fi
  results+=("$fanin|$name|$file|$kind|$rtype")
done

printf '%s\n' "${results[@]}" | sort -t'|' -k1,1nr | head -40 | while IFS='|' read -r fanin name file kind rtype; do
  if [[ "$kind" == "method" ]]; then sym="(${rtype}).${name}"; else sym="$name"; fi
  printf '%4d  %s  %s\n' "$fanin" "$sym" "$file"
done
BASHEOF

This method on the CEL filter engine in `internal/filter/` has the highest fan-in among `internal/` symbols I could measure reliably. It is declared here:

```73:80:internal/filter/engine.go
// CompileToStatement compiles and renders the filter in a single step.
func (e *Engine) CompileToStatement(ctx context.Context, filter string, opts RenderOptions) (Statement, error) {
	program, err := e.Compile(ctx, filter)
	if err != nil {
		return Statement{}, err
	}
	return program.Render(opts)
}
```

A repo-wide search for `.CompileToStatement(` finds **38** call sites. The next-highest reliably identifiable symbols are lower:

| Symbol | Path | Approx. fan-in |
|---|---|---|
| `NewEngine` | `internal/filter/engine.go` | ~32 |
| `GenUUID` | `internal/util/util.go` | ~28 |
| `addArg` (on `*renderer`) | `internal/filter/render.go` | ~28 |

Callers include filter tests under `internal/filter/`, production use in `internal/filter/helpers.go`, API validation in `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go` and `shortcut_service.go`, and memo-filter SQL generation in `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/memo_relation.go`.

**Caveat:** Go was not available here, so this is static text matching rather than a full call-graph analysis. Very common method names (e.g. `Len`, `Validate`) would over-count and were excluded; `CompileToStatement` is distinctive enough that the ~38 figure is trustworthy.
